newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan denies its troops clashed in north Uganda.
newsitem.headline: Sudan denies its troops clashed in north Uganda.

text.p: A Sudanese state minister denied on Tuesday that Sudan's troops clashed with Ugandan forces in northern Uganda, which Khartoum accuses of helping anti-government rebels in a war in the south.

"The charge is baseless," Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Mustafa Osman Ismail said on state radio. He accused Ugandan troops "of taking prisoner a number of Sudanese soldiers during their (Ugandan forces) attack on Yei and Kaia" in Sudan.

Ismail did not give a date. But Uganda on Friday said its army killed 60 Sudanese soldiers and captured more than 100 just inside Uganda, beating back a joint attack by the Sudanese army and Ugandan rebels.
Sudan accuses Ugandan troops of fighting alongside Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) rebels in the south, while Kampala accuses Khartoum of aiding the Ugandan rebels.

Forces under SPLA leader John Garang's command have stepped up their war to topple Khartoum's government. Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north.
Khartoum on Monday signed a deal with five former rebel factions which it hopes will be a solution to the conflict, but the accord does not include the SPLA.
